name: Multimodal intelligence & perception
question: What does the agent see, hear and understand?
description: VLM backbones, video understanding, semantic grounding, open-vocabulary perception and temporal scene understanding.

name: Spatial & physical grounding
question: Where are things, and how can they be interacted with?
description: 3D geometry, point clouds, object pose, scene graphs, affordances, contact and 4D spatial reasoning.

name: Embodied reasoning & planning
question: What should the robot do, and in what order?
description: Task decomposition, hierarchical planning, visual reasoning, memory, skill selection and recovery planning.

name: VLA architectures & action representations
question: How should executable actions be represented and generated?
description: Autoregressive policies, action tokens, diffusion, flow matching, latent actions and hierarchical control.

name: World models & predictive representations
question: How does the environment evolve under interventions?
description: Latent dynamics, video prediction, object-centric dynamics, physics-informed prediction and uncertainty-aware models.

name: World-Action Models
question: How should predicted futures influence action generation?
description: Joint or cascaded future-state and action generation, action-conditioned prediction, rollout scoring and WAM inference.

name: Data engines & pretraining
question: Where does embodied experience come from?
description: Robot demonstrations, human video, synthetic data, teleoperation, cross-embodiment transfer and data engines.

name: Policy learning, RL & adaptation
question: How do policies improve through experience?
description: Imitation learning, offline/online RL, rewards, preference learning, test-time adaptation and continual learning.

name: Sensors & robot embodiments
question: Which bodies and physical modalities are supported?
description: Tactile, force, proprioception, navigation, mobile manipulation, humanoids and dexterous robotics.

name: Systems, hardware & deployment
question: Can the model run fast and reliably on the robot?
description: Inference acceleration, quantization, token pruning, memory, scheduling, edge deployment and hardware/software co-design.

name: Evaluation, robustness & safety
question: How do we know it works outside the demo?
description: Benchmarks, distribution shifts, failure detection, calibration, safety constraints and real-world evaluation.
